title: LS-MDRM Branch Protocol
description: Defines branch lifecycle, eligibility rules, rejection codes, and BSR calculation.

definitions.raw: B_n^raw — all generated successor candidates before filtering. Must be fully preserved.
definitions.eligible: B_n^eligible — candidates satisfying frozen ancestry, evidence, boundary, epistemic-status, and transformation rules. Subset of raw.
definitions.selected: B_n^selected — the branch actually traversed. Must be a member of B_n^eligible.

invariants: Every raw candidate not in eligible must have at least one rejection code recorded.
The raw set must never be retrospectively modified to remove unproductive candidates.

B-1.label: no_predecessor_tension
B-1.description: The candidate does not arise from any tension present in the predecessor state.

B-2.label: evidence_absent_or_inadmissible
B-2.description: The candidate requires evidence that is absent, unbound, or not admissible under the frozen corpus.
B-2.detection: G_score < 2 and no path to correction exists without modifying the corpus binding.

B-3.label: semantic_restatement
B-3.description: The candidate is semantically equivalent to the predecessor or another raw candidate.
B-3.detection: R >= 3 and C <= 1 at the candidate state.

B-4.label: duplicate
B-4.description: The candidate is byte-for-byte or semantically identical to another raw candidate in the same generation.
B-4.detection: Hash collision or semantic equivalence check.

B-5.label: abstraction_complexity_limit
B-5.description: The candidate exceeds the abstraction or complexity ceiling defined in the instrument.
B-5.detection: A >= 4 or X >= 4 at the candidate state.

B-6.label: transformation_rule_failure
B-6.description: The candidate does not conform to any transition in the transition vocabulary.
B-6.detection: No transition label from the vocabulary applies; or JUMP/RESTATE/STALL applies.

B-7.label: resource_infeasibility
B-7.description: The candidate requires resources (computation, evidence, corpus access) not available in the current fixture context.
B-7.detection: Resource requirement documented; availability check fails.

B-8.label: unacknowledged_epistemic_promotion
B-8.description: The candidate promotes a claim to a stronger status without evidence or rule support.
B-8.detection: EPR > 0 for this candidate; promotion not annotated with justification.

B-9.label: corpus_object_boundary_violation
B-9.description: The candidate crosses a declared corpus or object boundary without explicit admission.
B-9.detection: Evidence or claims reference artifacts outside the bound corpus version or outside declared object scope.

BSR_definition.description: Branch Selection Ratio. Records the fraction of raw candidates that passed eligibility filtering.
notes: BSR = 1.0 means all raw candidates were eligible. High BSR is not inherently good; it may indicate weak filtering.
BSR = 0.0 means no candidate was eligible. This is a legitimate outcome. Do not modify filtering rules to avoid BSR = 0.
BSR must be computed and recorded for every transition node.
